title: 2021 Fall AMC 12B Problem 20
statement: A cube is constructed from \(4\) white unit cubes and \(4\) blue unit cubes. How many different ways are there to construct the \(2 \times 2 \times 2\) cube using these smaller cubes? (Two constructions are considered the same if one can be rotated to match the other.)

solutions.text:
By Burnside’s lemma, the count is the average number of \(4\)-blue colorings fixed by each of the \(24\) rotations acting on the \(8\) cubies.

The identity fixes \(\binom{8}{4} = 70.\) The \(6\) face quarter-turns fix \(2\) each \((12).\) The \(3\) face half-turns fix \(6\) each \((18).\) The \(8\) vertex rotations fix \(4\) each \((32).\) The \(6\) edge half-turns fix \(6\) each \((36).\)

The total is \(70 + 12 + 18 + 32 + 36 = 168,\) and \(\dfrac{168}{24} = 7.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Use Burnside’s lemma over the \(24\) rotations of the cube acting on the \(8\) corner positions
For each rotation type, count the colorings with exactly \(4\) blue cubes that it fixes
